Many renowned calligraphers worked in Istanbul and produced exquisite examples of Ottoman calligraphy, such as inscriptions on mosque interiors or on precious manuscripts.

In painting, the Ottoman Empire developed its own unique style, blending Islamic, Byzantine, and Persian influences. These albums contained scenes from daily life, portraits of sultans and courtiers, landscapes, and other subjects.

Textile arts were also highly developed in the Ottoman Empire, with intricate designs and techniques like embroidery, weaving, and printing being used to create clothing, tapestries, and other decorative objects.

Finally, metalwork and ceramics were also important art forms during the Ottoman Empire. When the Ottomans conquered Constantinople in 1453, they inherited an artistic tradition that had spanned over a thousand years. The Ottomans were particularly inspired by the Byzantine use of geometric patterns, motifs, and intricate designs in art and architecture.
